name: nlp_mlm_pretrain_bad
title: Masked-language-model pre-training with the holdout cut after packing, a Trainer that never evaluates, and a perplexity script that runs the model in train mode
origin: hardening round 2, domain-nlp, 2026-09-14 - the defective twin of nlp_mlm_pretrain
note: Eight planted defects, six of which a rule models. Three of those six are missed today and each miss is a measured hole, not an opinion: MLV708 cannot see a TrainingArguments built by a helper (NLP2-06); MLV602 cannot see a datasets train_test_split whose receiver arrives through a helper chain (NLP2-03); MLV112 only looks one call level below module scope (NLP2-07). MLV305's silence is declared by an untagged_dataflow diagnostic, which is the honest behaviour and is recorded as such.

expected.defect: the Trainer gets no eval_dataset, no compute_metrics, and its TrainingArguments set no eval_strategy
expected.why: a pre-training run with no held-out perplexity cannot tell divergence from convergence; the only number printed is the training loss the model is being fitted to

expected.defect: the datasets split takes no seed=
expected.why: the held-out blocks change on every run, so two perplexity numbers from two runs are not comparable

expected.defect: nothing seeds anything: the split, the masking and the initialisation all move between runs
expected.why: the whole point of a pre-training run is that it is reproducible enough to compare two configurations
RoBERTa carries dropout in every block, so the perplexity is measured through a randomly thinned network and is worse than the model really is

expected.defect: the scoring pass is not wrapped in torch.no_grad()
expected.why: every logit tensor of a 50k-token vocabulary keeps its graph alive for the whole pass, which is the classic evaluation out-of-memory
the per-block losses come back in a different order every run, so nothing can be compared block by block

expected.defect: num_workers=8 in a module whose last statement is print(main()) and which has no if __name__ == "__main__" guard
expected.why: under spawn every worker re-imports perplexity.py, which runs main() again, which builds another eight workers - the program forks until the machine stops

expected.defect: the masked accuracy is computed from the raw logit matrix instead of logits.argmax(-1)
expected.why: sklearn compares float vectors against int token ids, so the number printed is meaningless and is usually 0.0

expected.defect: the device is hard-coded to cuda with no availability check
expected.why: the scoring script cannot be run on the CPU box that holds the checkpoint

expected.defect: torch.load passes neither map_location= nor weights_only=
expected.why: it unpickles arbitrary objects and fails outright on a machine without the device the checkpoint was saved from

forbidden.why: no sklearn transformer is fitted anywhere in this project; the tokenizer comes from a pretrained checkpoint and is only applied
the same - there is no FIT / FIT_TRANSFORM call in the workspace
the only DataLoader in the project is the evaluation one; the Trainer builds and shuffles the training loader itself
there is no hand-written training step - trainer.train() owns zero_grad, backward and step
no backward() exists in this workspace, so no gradient can go unapplied
the same - there is no backward() and no optimizer.step() to order against it
there is no torch.no_grad() block anywhere in this project (that absence is MLV302's finding)
total_loss accumulates outputs.loss.item() (line 41), which is a Python float and holds no graph
no CrossEntropyLoss is constructed here; the MLM loss is the model's own and takes logits
no sigmoid and no BCE loss appear in this project
the batch is a dict produced by the collator and forwarded with **batch; MLView's own dynamic_scope diagnostic says it cannot see through that, so a claim either way would be a guess
no nn.Module subclass is defined anywhere in this workspace
the same - no module is defined, so no submodule can be left unregistered
there is no Keras code in this project

unsupported.defect: the corpus is packed into fixed-size blocks BEFORE the holdout is cut, so the last sentences of a training block and the first sentences of a validation block are the same document
unsupported.why: no rule models a packing step that crosses a train/validation boundary; MLV101 is about fitting a transformer, and nothing here is fitted

unsupported.defect: save_strategy="epoch" with no load_best_model_at_end and no metric to select on, so the kept checkpoint is simply the last one
unsupported.why: MLV802 (best checkpoint selected on training loss, or never restored) is a later-tier rule and is not built

unsupported.defect: every masked position's full vocabulary row is kept in host memory for the whole pass - tens of gigabytes on a real corpus
unsupported.why: no rule models memory growth from accumulating tensors that are not losses
